prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single part, B040, credited to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange did not weaken the scientific case, and no member disputed its core. Proglucagon processing, the active GLP-1(7-36) amide, its glucose-dependent insulinotropic and appetite actions in humans, and then receptor biology are an original and complete mechanistic chain. Independent randomized outcome trials for weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints confirm the clinical consequence, and the field is mature. The chair's questions are about attribution and framing rather than about whether the discovery is real. My answer is that the prize should honour the discovery of the hormone's actions, and that the citation should say so, naming the physiology and the active form and stating the therapeutic consequence as a result. Holst contributes the human physiology of the active peptide, Drucker the receptor biology, GLP-1 and GLP-2 actions and translation, and Mojsov the identification and synthesis of the active form. A single-achievement prize keeps all three places on one coherent discovery and avoids a division of the three-person limit that would weaken both parts.
statement.case_against: The weakness is still attribution, and nothing in round 1 resolved it. Mojsov's priority on the active peptide relative to the Habener-group work is credited but contested, and I cannot settle it from the supplied evidence or from memory; the other five members say the same. If the committee examined the primary literature and found her contribution subordinate, the third place would be open, and Knudsen would then be the natural candidate, which would shift the prize toward drug design. Excluding Knudsen is a framing judgement that can be criticised, because her long-acting analogues are what patients receive. I also accept the chair's point that unanimous agreement on the topic may mask different degrees of confidence in the exact trio, and mine is lower for the names than for the field. Finally, by holding B040 as a single part I leave the strongest basic-science alternative, B039, unrewarded this year, and I cannot claim that cost is zero.

responses.point: The chair answers my TOR comment by calling a Hall-centred B025 plausible and not premature but better kept for a later year, since Hall alone understates the chemical-biology route to the mammalian target and adding Schreiber or Sabatini invites a contested allocation.
responses.response: I accept most of this and have moved on B025. In round 1 I treated Hall-only as a clean fallback. After reading the chair and Wahren-Herlenius I think a Hall-only citation is too narrow, because it leaves out how the mammalian target and its complexes were identified, while a three-name set forces a judgement between yeast genetics, pharmacology and mammalian biochemistry that the supplied evidence does not let us make. That makes TOR a worse fallback than I said, and it is why B039 is now my clear first alternative. I do not agree that B039 belongs only to a later year, because its attribution is tidier than TOR's and its science is complete now.

responses.point: Perlmann calls the PERK branch a qualification rather than a disqualifier for Mori and Walter, and treats Hall plus one co-laureate as the other fallback.
responses.response: I agree the PERK branch qualifies B039 and does not disqualify it, and I still hold it as my fallback if B040 stalls. I would go a little further than you: the citation cannot say simply the unfolded protein response, because that would implicitly credit Ron, Harding and Kaufman's work to Walter and Mori. It would have to be limited to the signalling from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus through IRE1, HAC1 and XBP1. If the committee cannot accept that boundary, B039 weakens, and I would then rank B034 above it. On B025 I do not share your preference for Schreiber in the second slot, because I think the allocation problem remains unresolved and weighs against TOR this year.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius would state in the citation that excluding Knudsen is a judgement about what the discovery was, not about her importance, and she resists a four-name prize because the three-person limit would force out someone with a better claim to the physiology.
responses.response: I agree with both points and have adopted the framing in my citation, which names the physiology and the active form and describes the therapy as the consequence. I also share your resistance to a four-name configuration, which the limit forbids anyway. Where I differ is on UPR versus CAR-T as my first alternative. You weigh demonstrated clinical outcome and autoimmune movement heavily, and I accept that CAR-T meets that test better than B039. But the attribution gap, Eshhar being absent from the credited names, weighs on a CAR-T citation in the same way as the PERK branch weighs on B039. Because of that I treat them as nearly equal fallbacks, with B039 first on credit cleanliness and B034 second on clinical effect.

responses.point: Linnarsson says that if the committee rewarded drug development, Knudsen would join Drucker and Holst and Mojsov would drop out, and that this harder case blurs the priority of the discovery; he also keeps B008 and B034 as alternatives and not as second parts.
responses.response: This is the right way to state the contingency, and I agree with it. If the committee decides that the analogue design is decisive, the discovery framing is lost and the prize becomes a different one, so I would not simply swap Knudsen for Mojsov inside the physiology citation. The contested priority would matter less in that version, but the credit would then be for a therapy, and I prefer the physiology prize. I also agree that a second part for B008 or B034 would divide the three places and thin the GLP-1 credit. I add that B008 has, in my view, the least tractable attribution on the shortlist, with six names for three places, so I keep it off my alternatives.

responses.point: El-Manira says a clean credit should not decide ranking by itself, and that the demonstrated change in medicine is far larger for GLP-1 than for the unfolded protein response, whose reach into patient outcomes is indirect.
responses.response: I agree that credit cleanliness alone should not decide a ranking, and my own ranking of B040 first rests on the size of its demonstrated effect on medicine as well as on the quality of the science. That is why B039 is a fallback and not a competitor to B040 in my view. I disagree only mildly on the weight of indirect reach. For the physiology or medicine remit, a discovery that explains a core cellular mechanism can be recognised before its therapeutic consequences are fully realised, and the Nobel tradition has done that. That is a reason to hold B039 as a serious alternative, not a reason to rank it above incretin biology this year.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contribution to the active GLP-1 peptide is established strongly enough relative to the Habener group, and I cannot adjudicate this from the supplied evidence.

Whether the committee, on examining the literature, would judge drug design to be decisive and replace one of the three names with Knudsen, which would change the prize from a physiology prize to a therapy prize.
Whether a B039 citation limited to the IRE1, HAC1 and XBP1 arm can be defended given the PERK and ATF6 contributions of others outside the credited names.
Whether B034 would be mature enough and its credit adequate, with Eshhar absent and solid-tumour and safety questions open, if B040 stalled.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson, who sits on the committee, and with Jonas Frisen outside it, and we share the Karolinska Institutet setting; none of the credited names for B040, B039 or B034 is involved, and shared affiliation does not establish a tie to any candidate. My disclosure is unchanged from round 1.
